amended: 2026-11-06, after the plan (288d1eaa) and BEFORE any development fit was run or any Exhaustion Land Phase II yield was read. Nothing had been scored.
reason: The plan used the existing Hargreaves PET directly as RothC's 0.75 x open-pan evaporation. RothC's own Rothamsted example (RothC_description.pdf, TSMD table) gives 0.75 x pan = 448 mm/yr (July 77 mm); the 1878-1907 Hargreaves mean is 717 mm/yr (July 126 mm), about 1.6x higher. A first spin-up check (no yields involved) gave 45.7 t active C/ha under RothC's documented 1.70 t C/ha/yr Hoosfield input, against the 31.1 t (33.8 - 2.7 IOM) RothC reports: the excess evaporation slows decomposition. The same bias depresses drainage (development diagnostic: ~94 mm/yr against drain gauges' roughly half of rainfall).
change: Monthly evapotranspiration for RothC's moisture factor AND for the dual-ledger drainage = Hargreaves(year, month) x r_month, r_month = 0.75 x RothC's Rothamsted open-pan mean / the 1878-1907 Hargreaves mean for that month. The same factors apply at Woburn (its weather is Rothamsted's, a declared proxy). The production climate potential A0 is unchanged (it remains the existing production response).
source: RothC_description.pdf (Coleman and Jenkinson), section 1.6 table 'Accumulated Topsoil Moisture Deficit for Rothamsted': open-pan evaporation 8, 10, 27, 49, 83, 99, 103, 91, 69, 34, 16, 8 mm
